Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: A friend on their way to the airport calls, thinking they left their passport at home, and asks if you can check and bring it to them right away.
Expectation2: Greet clients and make them feel comfortable
Situation2: A familiar customer strolls in while the receptionist is free to chat.
Story: I was just finishing up sweeping the salon floor when my phone buzzed. It was Mia, my oldest friend, her voice frantic. “I think I left my passport at home! I’m almost at the airport—can you check and bring it if it’s there? Please, I’ll miss my flight!” My heart raced. Of course, I wanted to help her; that’s what friends do, especially in emergencies. But as I glanced up, Mrs. Patel, my regular client, walked in, her face lighting up when she saw me. She always expected a warm greeting and a few minutes of friendly conversation before her appointment. The receptionist was free, but Mrs. Patel always preferred me. I could feel the weight of both expectations pressing down on me—Mia’s desperate need and Mrs. Patel’s anticipation of our usual welcome. My mind spun, torn between rushing out to help my friend and staying to fulfill my professional duty, knowing that either choice would let someone down.
